title: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
key_facts: Anthropic launched a service called OSS Scanner for open-source projects.
Projects that opt in get periodic security scans by Anthropic's strongest models, including Claude Mythos, at no cost.
Reports are fully model-generated, without human review or triage, so some may be incorrect or invalid.
The Verge notes AI tools have helped find major open-source flaws, such as the 'Copy Fail' bug that affected nearly every Linux distribution in May.
Some open-source projects, including Linus Torvalds and Google, are struggling with the flood of AI-generated bug reports.
quote_evidence: It says open-source projects that opt-in will get “thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.”
The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage.
why_it_matters_hint: Maintainers may learn of flaws sooner but must check unreviewed AI reports themselves.
notes: Read The Verge text (short). Anthropic's own page not opened; The Verge quotes Anthropic's statement.
